Quick Read

Anthropic sold 980 million Class A shares at $83 on Nov. 18, above its marketed range of $70 to $78, raising $81.3 billion ($93.5 billion if underwriters buy all 147 million extra shares), the largest IPO on record. It opened at $111.50 and closed its first day on the Nasdaq as ANT at $97.17, up 17% from the offer price. Warren Buffett told CNBC in 2019 that in 54 years Berkshire had never bought a new issue; Berkshire's one exception since was Snowflake's 2020 IPO at the offer price.

From their first-day closes, five of the six biggest tech IPOs since Facebook (Facebook, Alibaba, Uber, Snowflake, Rivian) were lower six months later and trailed the S&P 500; three lost more than half within a year; only Arm rose. $10,000 in each ($60,000) was worth $53,654 at six months against $64,110 in the index, and pulled level only at three years.

SpaceX, the live analog, closed its first day at $160.95, fell to $108.27 by Aug. 5 and trades about $138, 14% below its first close, with up to 797.6 million shares (about $110 billion) unlocking Dec. 8.

For a retiree with $2.4 million who wants $10,000 of Anthropic (about 103 shares at the first-day close): the worst six-month path on the list (Rivian) would cost $7,738; size the position for that case, and note that the IPO-price allocation, not the open, is where the first-day pop has gone in six of seven cases.

A 67-year-old retired engineer with $2.4 million in a rollover IRA wants to put $10,000 into Anthropic (NASDAQ: ANT) now that it trades, and he has company. Anthropic sold 980 million shares at $83 each on Nov. 18, above its marketed range of $70 to $78, raising $81.3 billion, the largest IPO on record, ahead of Elon Musk's SpaceX (NASDAQ: SPCX), which listed in June. The stock opened at $111.50 on Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT and closed its first day at $97.17, up 17% from the offer price. Up to 20% of the deal was set aside for individual investors through their brokers. Everyone else paid the market price, and the first-day close is where the history below starts.

Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL), the search, advertising, cloud, and AI platforms provider, closed at $272.66, down 3.46%. Anthropic's Nasdaq debut and Google's Blue Origin partnership update were cited as catalysts, while investors are watching how AI-linked valuation gains affect Alphabet's investment portfolio.
Trading volume reached 48.1 million shares, coming in about 58% above its three-month average of 30.4 million shares. Alphabet IPO'd in 2004 and has grown 10,763% since going public.

How the markets moved today

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) closed at 7,176, down 2.02%, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) closed at 23,879, down 2.25%. Among internet media and digital advertising peers, Meta Platforms closed at $596.22, down 3.27%, and Amazon.com closed at $257.37, down 3.87%, showing broad pressure across large-cap AI and cloud names.

What this means for investors

Anthropic's market debut and IPO pricing put fresh value on Alphabet's nearly 14% stake. The Google parent already owns close to its 15% ownership cap, which is now worth about $175 billion based on Anthropic's initial closing price.

In other news, Google has picked Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket to launch data center satellites for its Project Suncatcher program in 2029, the company said today.

Google first revealed its plans to run AI systems in space through orbiting data centers about a year ago, calling the effort one of its research "moonshots." That project will garner investor attention, but Anthropic's debut was the focus today. Given Alphabet's meaningful ownership, it's likely that some investors pulled money from that stock to buy Anthropic today.

Inside Brad Gerstner's Portfolio: Every Move He Made in the Third Quarter ©Alexander's Images and View more by inkdrop via Canva
Key Takeaways

Brad Gerstner's Altimeter Capital opened a $680 million Tesla position in the third quarter, added to Meta Platforms and Micron, and sold out of Qualcomm and Applied Materials.

Tesla trades at about 180x forward earnings, and analysts' average target is just 7% above the price, so the new stake is a bet on Robotaxi profits that the estimates don't show yet.

Meta trades at about 19x forward earnings, below its own five-year average, and it's the move the numbers back best.

Qualcomm's falling estimates back that exit, while Applied Materials' estimates have risen even as its stock halved after Sept. 30.

Brad Gerstner's Altimeter Capital ended the third quarter with a brand-new stake in Tesla (TSLA:NASDAQ) and four fewer chip stocks, according to its 13F for the quarter ended Sept. 30, filed Nov. 16. It also added to Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ) and Micron (MU:NASDAQ), and sold out of Qualcomm (QCOM:NASDAQ) and Applied Materials (AMAT:NASDAQ), among others.

Tesla is the big new bet, and the priciest

Altimeter, which manages $18.75 billion in all, held $9.80 billion of US stocks in just 16 positions on Sept. 30. Tesla went straight to No. 4 on that list: 1.92 million shares worth $680 million, or 6.9% of its 13F stocks, in a stock Altimeter didn't own on June 30. Tesla is up 8% since Sept. 30, the only one of the quarter's three buys in the green.

That's a lot to pay, though. Tesla trades at about 180x forward earnings, well above its five-year quarter-end average of 112x. Its GAAP operating margin was 2.6% in the third quarter, down from 5.8% a year earlier, as R&D spending rose 69%. Tesla has guided 2026 capital spending to about $20 billion, more than double 2025's $8.5 billion, and analysts expect its free cash flow to stay negative through 2028. Anyone buying at this price is betting on Robotaxi, and CEO Elon Musk has said Robotaxi revenue should become noticeable by the second quarter of 2027.

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Tesla, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Tesla's Analyst Ratings

More Meta, at a discount to its own history

Altimeter added 25% to Meta in the quarter, ending it with 1.70 million shares worth $1.23 billion. That's 12.6% of its 13F stocks and its second-largest position. The stock has fallen 15% since Sept. 30, but the business is still growing fast: third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion. At about 19x forward earnings, Meta trades below its five-year quarter-end average of 21x.

title: Daniel Loeb's Meta Stock Bet Stands Out as Tiger Global Trims
detail:
Daniel Loeb's Meta Stock Bet Stands Out as Tiger Global Trims
Moz Farooque ACCA
Thu, November 19, 2026 at 10:42 AM PST 2 min read
META
NVDA
MSFT
AMZN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Two hedge funds took different positions on Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) in the third quarter. Daniel Loeb (Trades, Portfolio)'s Third Point disclosed a 655,000-share stake, making Meta its largest publicly reported holding by value at quarter-end. Chase Coleman (Trades, Portfolio)'s Tiger Global cut its stake by about 20% and still held more than three times as many shares as Third Point. The filings offer a view of how each fund sized its Meta exposure as the company ramped up spending on artificial intelligence.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with META.

Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

META GF Value chart

Third Point's position was worth approximately $475 million on Sept. 30, or just over 10% of the holdings it publicly reported. The fund also disclosed positions in Nvidia and Microsoft, and it dropped Amazon from its reported holdings during the quarter. Tiger Global reduced its Meta stake by nearly 575,000 shares, leaving about 2.25 million shares worth $1.63 billion at quarter-end. Meta still ranked third among its disclosed U.S. stock holdings by quarter-end market value.

Both firms filed their quarterly disclosures on Nov. 16. The figures capture holdings as of Sept. 30 and give no explanation for the trades. Reuters reported that Loeb told investors in November that Third Point had reduced exposure to large cloud companies and businesses tied to semiconductors and data centers. He did not identify the specific holdings he cut, leaving Third Point's current Meta position unclear.

Investors Takeaway

Meta's third-quarter results show why the spending question matters. Revenue rose 26% year over year to $64.6 billion. The company generated $32.79 billion in operating cash flow and spent $34.91 billion on capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases. That left it with negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion for the quarter. Meta expects 2026 capital expenditures of $135 billion to $145 billion on the same basis.

Management says AI is already helping the advertising business by improving recommendations, engagement and monetization. It expects newer AI initiatives to take longer to generate returns and says it plans to keep investing aggressively in 2027 as it develops its budget.

For shareholders, the next earnings update will put Meta's spending to the test. Watch whether advertising revenue and operating cash flow can grow fast enough to cover the rising cost of building and running AI infrastructure. The amount Meta commits to spending in 2027, and what management can show for that investment in its existing advertising business, will help investors gauge when stronger sales might translate into more free cash flow.

detail:

Nebius (NBIS) stock's Q3 sell-off looks like an attractive opportunity, with shares down almost 64% from their 52-week high. The artificial intelligence (AI) cloud infrastructure provider disappointed investors with another capacity delay, but the underlying business momentum tells a very different story. Rather than pulling back, customers are locking in much larger, multi-year commitments. As CEO Arkady Volozh emphasized on the earnings call, "The demand for AI is real and substantial."

Q3 2026 revenue surged 571%, and new contract economics improved. I understand the concerns about financing this enormous expansion. Yet customers' willingness to help fund it makes me more confident. Thus, I rate NBIS stock a Buy.

A Strong Quarter Got Overshadowed

Nebius' strong Q3 results got overshadowed by another capacity delay. Investors were already questioning Neocloud financing and the sustainability of AI spending. Nebius then shifted some expected revenue into early 2027 because third-party capacity was delayed. Management now expects 2026 revenue near the low end of its $3.0–$3.4 billion range.

Its $7 billion-plus annualized revenue milestone moves from December to February. That is disappointing, although the customer contracts behind the delayed capacity remain intact.

More importantly, the company showed considerable progress. Revenue reached $980.8 million, up 68% sequentially, while AI Cloud revenue grew 643% year-over-year. Group adjusted EBITDA reached $465.8 million, and AI Cloud's adjusted EBITDA margin was 53.2%. Annualized revenue run rate rose 113% sequentially to $6.4 billion.

Q3 included $325 million of nonrecurring partner revenue. Excluding that contribution, revenue still exceeded four times last year's total. Customers have also signed over $12 billion of contract value since Q3 began.

The improving contract terms are what impressed me most. Prepayments on Q3 contracts lasting at least a year covered more than 100% of associated capex. That compares with 50%–60% in Q2. Management's revenue-based payback estimate for comparable contracts improved to 19 months from 22 months. Customers are signing longer agreements at higher prices, helping Nebius recover its spending faster.
